register.labelZh: WANT 片語動詞的實際用途
register.summaryZh: want for nothing 可以用簡潔而較正式的方式,表示某人擁有所需的食物、衣物、照顧或支援。；want in 和 want in on something 可用來表示想加入團隊、項目、遊戲或計劃。；want out 和 want out of something 可清楚表示不想再留在小組、項目或協議之中。；Want in? 和 I want out 是較口語而直接的說法;want for 則較常見於正式文字。
register.summaryEn: Want for nothing is a concise, formal way to say that someone has all the food, clothing, care or support they need. Want in and want in on something are useful when you want to join a team, project, game or plan. Want out and want out of something make it easy to express that you no longer wish to stay in a group, project or agreement. Want in? and I want out are common, direct forms in informal speech, while want for often appears in more formal writing.

fixedVariable.variableZh: 情境清楚時,want in 本身已完整。如要說明想加入甚麼,可用 want in on + 計劃、項目或活動。I want in. / I want in on the project.；情境清楚時,want out 本身已完整。如要說明想退出甚麼,可用 want out of + 小組、計劃或協議。She wants out. / She wants out of the agreement.；want for 較正式,尤其常見於否定意思,例如 want for nothing、never want for anything;也可直接指出缺少的東西。They want for nothing. / The village may want for clean water.
fixedVariable.variableEn: Want in is complete when the situation is clear. Use want in on + a plan, project or activity when you name what the person wants to join. Want out is complete when the situation is clear. Use want out of + a group, plan or agreement when you name what the person wants to leave. Want for is more formal and is especially common in negative ideas: want for nothing, never want for anything. It can also name something that is missing.
